intro: Sunny Vancouver morning; City Hall's election outcome awaits certification; AI security and infrastructure costs dominate the tech and markets conversation. Your Tuesday briefing, compiled October 20.

weather.title: Sunny · 8°C this morning
weather.summary: Today sunny, 15°/7°C, dry. Wednesday 16°/8°C with increasing cloud and possible rain overnight. Thursday partly sunny 13°/7°C; Friday 13°/7°C, rain risk overnight.

stories.title: Vancouver election: final declaration due tomorrow
stories.summary: Unofficial results show Pete Fry leading the mayoral vote with 98,494. Official results and plebiscite decisions are expected Wednesday, October 21, by 4 PM.

stories.title: US federal agencies ordered to remove DeepSeek technology
stories.summary: DHS directed federal civilian systems to remove DeepSeek products and affected third-party services, citing supply-chain and data security. China has challenged the move. Important distinction: this is a US federal procurement restriction, not a general ban on running local models.

stories.title: Amazon targets CUDA lock-in with TorchNeuron
stories.summary: Amazon says its new open-source TorchNeuron software enables PyTorch workloads to run on Trainium chips with fewer modifications. Watch whether alternative accelerators really become practical for model training.

stories.title: Inflation and oil put renewed pressure on equity markets
stories.summary: TSX opened 0.22% lower at 35,849.64, with miners weak and inflation concerns persisting. US futures were softer before the open. Intraday levels can change.

stories.title: Physical AI gets another push from Nvidia's industrial pitch
stories.summary: Jensen Huang urged German manufacturers to apply AI to physical industries and robotics rather than view it as a replacement for manufacturing. Relevant to the robotics tooling and edge-compute ecosystem.
